method: Author tree from `git archive 4ec961e`. For each mutant: built from a pristine copy of aisef2/app/lineage.py via validation.v2.mutation.mutants(src, 'child_evidence', _enum_members(src, pathlib.Path('.')))[INDEX], desc asserted == the batch entry, written over aisef2/app/lineage.py in a run-copy tree, then the one REGISTERED kill file run one mutant at a time from the copy root: nice -n 19 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -P -B -m unittest tests.v2.test_v21_pw_lineage_unread -q, under env -i with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin (stripped of /Users/nghinh/.opencode/bin and /Users/nghinh/.npm-global/bin, the two dirs holding an opencode executable), HOME and TMPDIR under the run tree, PYTHONPATH=<run root> (needed because -P keeps cwd off sys.path). Actual operator `why` strings per branch captured by calling lineage.child_evidence on crafted children (not_text, journal-path-is-a-directory, not-a-journal, torn-first-line) for baseline and each mutant.
measurement_result: Baseline 39 tests OK. Each of the 10 mutants: 39 tests OK == SURVIVED by measurement, matching the campaign. No REFUTED-by-measurement. All 10 mutate only the second element of the (state, detail) tuple (the UNREAD `why` prose); the first element and all control flow are untouched, so every STATE assertion (test_the_state_is_unread_and_never_unbegun) and the truthiness assertion (sup['unread'] in test_the_operator_may_supersede_by_the_claims_sha256_and_only_by_it) pass unchanged. The one content test, ChildThatCannotBeRead.test_the_refusal_says_what_could_not_be_read_and_what_the_operator_may_do, pins 'PermissionError'+JOURNAL.name through claim()'s refusal for the journal-locked L189 case only; every mutant either preserves that token (37/38/39/40 keep type(e).__name__='PermissionError') or is on another branch, so none is killed. Every mutant keeps the detail non-empty, so truthiness holds.

entries.grounds: L200, the 'holds bytes and no complete event' branch (reconstruct succeeds, events==[]: a torn/truncated first line). Measured on the torn_first_line fixture (self.put_journal(a_journal()[:60])): baseline why='aisef-run.jsonl holds bytes and no complete event (a first line that was cut)'; mutant why='aisef-run.jsonl' — the entire cause is gone, the detail collapses to the bare journal name. The operator then reads in claim()'s refusal '...cannot be read (aisef-run.jsonl): it may have begun (UNREAD)...', which says nothing about WHY and is in fact misleading here: this journal opens, decodes as text and reconstructs — it is not unreadable, it was cut mid-write, so the run truly began and the operator should continue from it, not restore permissions/encoding. The detail can no longer be told apart from the L186/L189/L197 causes. Kill file: baseline 39 OK, mutant 39 OK (SURVIVED); no test asserts this branch's detail. The campaign SURVIVED is explained by that coverage gap — the sibling L189 case has a 'PermissionError' content test, L200 has none (an asymmetric gap).

entries.refutation: Input: a child whose journal run/journals/aisef-run.jsonl holds a torn first line and no complete event — the test's existing variant `torn_first_line`: self.put_journal(a_journal()[:60]). Reader: the operator reading claim()'s LineageRefused `({unread})` (lineage.py:318-324), continue_from's report 'why' (bundle_cli.py:896), the CONTINUED-BY.{n}.json 'unread' record (lineage.py:331), and the spend 'unaccounted' line (lineage.py:519-523). Sketch: in ChildThatCannotBeRead add a content test (sibling to test_the_refusal_says_what_could_not_be_read...) that builds the torn-first-line child and asserts state,why = lineage.child_evidence(child); self.assertEqual(state, lineage.UNREAD); self.assertIn(lineage.JOURNAL.name, why); self.assertRegex(why, r'holds bytes|complete event|first line'). Baseline why contains 'no complete event' (PASS); mutant-34 why='aisef-run.jsonl' lacks it (FAIL) — kills index 34. It pins content the reader relies on to tell a cut journal (continue from it) from an unreadable one (restore it); it is the symmetric completion of the coverage the L189 case already has, not padding.

entries.grounds: L189 `e.strerror or e` -> `e.strerror and e`. A real OS-raised OSError on this branch (IsADirectoryError / PermissionError / NotADirectoryError / ENAMETOOLONG / EIO) always has a truthy strerror, so `and` returns e and the detail renders str(e) instead of e.strerror. Measured (dir in the journal's place): baseline '...cannot be read (IsADirectoryError: Is a directory)'; mutant '...cannot be read (IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: <path>)' — MORE informative (errno + path), never less. The only way to get less (literal 'None') needs strerror falsy, which does not occur for OS-raised errors here. SURVIVED (39/39).

Input: the existing torn_first_line fixture, self.put_journal(a_journal()[:60]). Reader: the operator reading claim()'s LineageRefused ({unread}) at lineage.py:318-324, continue_from's report 'why' at bundle_cli.py:896, the CONTINUED-BY.{n}.json 'unread' record at lineage.py:331, and the spend 'unaccounted' line at lineage.py:519-523. Assertions: state,why = lineage.child_evidence(child); self.assertEqual(state, lineage.UNREAD); self.assertIn(lineage.JOURNAL.name, why); self.assertRegex(why, r'holds bytes|complete event|first line'). This kills index 34 (baseline why has 'no complete event'; mutant why is 'aisef-run.jsonl'). It is the symmetric completion of the content coverage the L189 case already has (the 'PermissionError' assertion at line 235-236); the L186/L189/L197 label mutants (35/37/41) are NOT owed tests because each keeps a unique interpolated diagnostic (e.reason / type(e).__name__ / str(e)) that still names the cause — adding tests for them would be reaching for a number.
notes: Target aisef2/app/lineage.py::child_evidence; snapshot 4ec961e. All 10 NEW survivors mutate only the UNREAD detail — the second element of the (state, detail) tuple — on child_evidence's four 'evidence there and unreadable' branches: L186 (UnicodeDecodeError), L189 (OSError not not_there), L197 (reconstruct raises), L200 (bytes but no complete event). Nine empty a string fragment; one (index 40) swaps `or`->`and` in the embedded OSError rendering. None changes the STATE (first element), the branch taken, or any value a decision keys on, so child_state(), continued_by(), claim()'s supersession, continue_from and the spend accounting all decide unchanged — which is why they survived. The ONE registered kill file (V21_TARGETS['...::child_evidence'] = ['tests/v2/test_v21_pw_lineage_unread.py']) was RUN against each mutant one at a time from a run-copy tree (PATH stripped of the two dirs holding an opencode executable, HOME/TMPDIR under the tree, PYTHONPATH=run root): baseline 39 OK; each mutant 39 OK => all SURVIVE by measurement, matching the campaign; NO REFUTED-by-measurement. Actual operator `why` strings were captured by calling child_evidence on crafted children for baseline and each mutant. Classification follows the owner rule ('a string read by an operator or a verifier is not harmless') and the W2-lineage-2 precedent (whole-cause loss with an uncovered symmetric sibling => REFUTED; redundant connective/label/space, or a not-less-informative rendering => AUDITED): 1 REFUTED (34) — the only mutant whose detail loses every word of the cause and collapses to the bare journal name 'aisef-run.jsonl', which the readers' generic 'cannot be read' wrapper then misdescribes (a torn/cut journal that in fact reads is not unreadable: the operator should continue from it, not restore it); 9 AUDITED (35,37,41 empty a label but keep the branch's unique interpolated diagnostic; 36,38,39,42,43 drop a paren or ': ' separator; 40 renders the OSError via str(e), errno and path included, never less). The four readers of the detail, confirmed by grep: claim()'s refusal (lineage.py:311,318-324), the supersedes 'unread' record in CONTINUED-BY.{n}.json (lineage.py:331), continue_from's report 'why' (bundle_cli.py:896), and account_of's spend 'unaccounted' line (lineage.py:518-523); the detail is never machine-parsed — every decision keys on the STATE, which every mutant preserves.
